test_title: PYST 60: RRB Group D - Mathematics (Held On: 23 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: Two pipes can fill a cistern, individually, in 96 min and 64 min, respectively. There is a pipe located at the bottom of the cistern to empty it. If all the three pipes are opened simultaneously, then the empty cistern gets filled in 48 min. How long will the pipe at the bottom of the tank take to empty the completely filled cistern if no other pipe is then open?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity of cistern = LCM of 96, 64, and 48 = 192 units.

Efficiency of the two filling pipes = 192 ÷ 96 = +2 units/min, and 192 ÷ 64 = +3 units/min.

Combined efficiency of all three pipes = 192 ÷ 48 = +4 units/min.

Efficiency of the emptying pipe = 4 − (2 + 3) = −1 unit/min.

**∴ The correct answer is 192 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A to fill the cistern = 96 min

Time taken by Pipe B to fill the cistern = 64 min

Time taken when all three pipes (A, B, and emptying Pipe C) are open = 48 min

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Time × Efficiency

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time (min)**
 **Total Work (Units)**
 **Efficiency (Units/min)**
 
 

 Pipe A (Fill)
 96
 192
 +2
 
 

 Pipe B (Fill)
 64
 +3
 
 

 A + B + C
 48
 +4
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of the emptying Pipe C be −x units/min.

⇒ Combined efficiency = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B − Efficiency of C

⇒ 4 = 2 + 3 − x

⇒ x = 5 − 4 = 1 unit/min

⇒ Time taken by Pipe C to empty the completely filled cistern = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of Pipe C

⇒ Time = 192 ÷ 1 = 192 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 192 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Concept

If a pipe fills a tank in x hours, its efficiency is +1/x per hour. If it empties the tank in y hours, its efficiency is −1/y per hour.

Work and Wages

Wages are strictly distributed in direct proportion to the amount of work done, which corresponds to the ratio of their efficiency if they work for the same duration.

Alternate Days Working

When individuals work on alternate days, calculate the total work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 workers) to approach the total capacity before adding individual days.
